chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Aban narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ismail ibn Sa'id from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A man asked him and said: 'May Allah improve you, is drinking wine worse or leaving the prayer?' He said: 'Drinking wine.' Then he said: 'And do you know why?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Because he enters a state in which he does not recognize his Lord.'
ai.seo_question: Why is drinking wine considered worse than missing prayer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Thawab al-A'mal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prioritizes the consumption of wine over the omission of prayer, a striking comparison that highlights the destructive nature of intoxication. He explains that wine induces a state of spiritual blindness where one loses cognizance of their Lord, effectively nullifying the inner presence required for valid worship. This underscores the Shia scholarly view that while prayer is a pillar, the loss of divine awareness through intoxication represents a more profound disconnection from God.
